title: Portrait and Harvest
premise: Folklorist Theo Zhou arrives in the dying village of Harrow's Bend to record its funeral songs, only to find that every resident signs a strange 'harvest paper' before leaving and that his own sleep recordings capture a second voice answering questions he never asked aloud. The voice belongs to the village itself, which has been counting its people for generations and will not release the last name on its ledger. As Theo digs into the fate of a folklorist who vanished there in 1974, he realizes the papers don't transfer property—they transfer identity, and staying invisible has made him the perfect final resident. In the end, Theo tricks the count by recording his family's names into the village's own song, giving it more voices than it can hold, and walks out at dawn with the last unsigned paper burning in his hand while the village forgets itself behind him.
about_author: Sable Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing oral histories from depopulated farming towns before turning to fiction. They write horror about places that remember people better than people remember themselves, and they still count the doors before bed.

chapters.title: The Song You Don't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Theo Zhou, POV. Theo arrives in Harrow's Bend with recording equipment and a grant to document its harvest dirge; the innkeeper sings one verse, goes pale, and refuses the second. That night Theo counts eleven doors in the inn though the building has seven rooms. Emotional beat: unease dressed as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. He maps the village and finds every household keeps a door-count ritual at dusk, tapping each frame with a knuckle. Old Marta Voss tells him the count must always come out even or someone 'owes.' His own rented cottage counts thirteen. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath scholarly routine.

chapters.title: The Harvest Paper
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At the county office Theo photographs the mysterious 'harvest papers'—documents transferring not land but 'name, voice, and remainder'—signed by every departing resident. The clerk's drawer holds an unsigned paper dated 1974, blank where a name should be. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Reviewing his sleep-recording app out of boredom, Theo hears himself ask questions in his sleep—who signed, who stayed—and a low second voice answering each one correctly. It knows things about 1974 no living villager has told him. Emotional beat: violation and fascination intertwined.

chapters.title: What Marta Kept
chapters.summary: Marta Voss, POV. Marta remembers the 1974 folklorist, Elias Brandt, who got too curious and became the village's 'keeper'—the name the count holds onto. She warns Theo that the papers aren't contracts but invitations, and that the village chooses who reads them as signatures. Emotional beat: guilt and protective urgency.

chapters.title: Calling Home
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo tries to bring his sister Lena and her son Sam to help him leave, but the roads loop back to the bend no matter the direction taken. The second voice, now speaking during his waking hours, explains gently: the count isn't finished, and unfinished counts keep what they've started counting. Emotional beat: trapped panic managed by cold analysis.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. In the chapel basement Theo finds Elias Brandt's tape reels: decades of recordings of the second voice, which is the accumulated chorus of everyone the village ever harvested. Among them he finds his own grandmother's maiden name—the reason the village reached for him. Emotional beat: grief reframing horror as inheritance.

chapters.title: Signing Season
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena and Sam arrive through the fog uninvited, and the village turns warmly hospitable—too warm—as residents begin pressing a fresh harvest paper toward Sam, the youngest name left to sign. Theo realizes the last resident signing triggers the count's completion. Emotional beat: maternal ferocity against polite menace.

chapters.title: The Counting Song
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Climax. On harvest night Theo plays all of Brandt's reels at once through the village loudspeakers, layering hundreds of harvested voices over the dirge until the count loses track of whose name belongs to whom. The doors swing open on their hinges; the papers blacken. Emotional beat: desperate, sacrificial defiance becoming release.

chapters.title: Remainder
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At dawn the three walk out past fields gone gray and houses standing empty of memory, the last unsigned paper crumbling in Theo's fist. In the car, Sam hums a verse of the dirge he never learned, and Theo lets him sing it twice. Emotional beat: hard-won peace shadowed by what they carry out with them.
